chunks: And said: 'I am sick (of what you worship)!'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Ibrahim mean when he said 'I am sick' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this declaration by Ibrahim (AS) serves as a rhetorical device to excuse himself from participating in the idolatrous festivities of his people, highlighting the disconnect between the monotheist and the polytheists. Shia exegetes often view this 'illness' not merely as physical but as a spiritual malady of the heart caused by deviation from Tawhid, positioning Ibrahim as the archetype of the pure believer. This verse underscores the necessity of distancing oneself from corrupt religious practices to maintain spiritual integrity.
